chunks.title: Drain leakage: IDSS
chunks.text: For the 2N7000, zero-gate-voltage drain current IDSS is specified at VDS = 48 V and VGS = 0 V. The maximum is 1 microampere under the table's default 25°C conditions. The elevated-temperature row has a different limit.
chunks.tags: idss off state drain source leakage zero gate voltage

chunks.title: Gate leakage: IGSS
chunks.text: Gate-body leakage IGSS is distinct from IDSS. The 2N7000 row uses VDS = 0 V and VGS = ±15 V, with a ±10 nA limit. Do not substitute drain-leakage conditions.
chunks.tags: igss gate body leakage gate current

chunks.title: Threshold voltage
chunks.text: For 2N7000 threshold voltage VGS(th), the table uses VDS = VGS and ID = 1 mA; the specified range is 0.8 to 3 V. This is not an off-state leakage test.

chunks.title: Device ratings
chunks.text: The drain-source absolute maximum rating is 60 V. An absolute maximum rating is not the IDSS measurement condition or a recommended operating target.

chunks.locator: Section · Settling Time and Timing Menu Settings
chunks.title: Allow the measurement to settle
chunks.text: Settling depends on source resistance and shunt capacitance from cables, fixtures, switches, and probes. Determine the delay experimentally using current versus time at the intended bias.
chunks.tags: settle settling delay stabilize time rc transient

chunks.title: Separate fixture leakage
chunks.text: Guarding reduces unwanted leakage through insulation. Verify the complete measurement circuit, including cables and fixtures; fixture leakage can contaminate device-current readings.
chunks.tags: guard guarding triax fixture insulation parasitic leakage

chunks.title: Control electrostatic interference
chunks.text: Shield sensitive circuitry and avoid nearby movement. The 4200A-SCS example connects its shield to Force LO; follow the particular instrument manual for connections.
chunks.tags: shield shielding noise movement electrostatic interference

chunks.title: Measure the system baseline
chunks.text: Measure instrument offsets, then add circuit components progressively with the DUT absent. Repeat at the intended test voltage to reveal leakage in cables and fixtures.
chunks.tags: offset baseline open circuit background calibration

chunks.locator: Section · Settling Time and Timing Menu Settings
chunks.title: Noise versus throughput
chunks.text: Additional filtering and delays can reduce noise while slowing measurements. A current-versus-time experiment helps choose a suitable interval.
chunks.tags: filter filtering average throughput speed noise tradeoff

chunks.title: Temperature and zero drift
chunks.text: Temperature and elapsed time can change zero offset. Stabilize the environment and follow the instrument's zero-correction procedure.
chunks.tags: drift temperature warmup zero correction stability

chunks.title: The reading includes error currents
chunks.text: Instrument input bias and currents generated by cables or insulators can contribute to the measured current. A measured value is not automatically the DUT leakage alone.
chunks.tags: bias generated triboelectric cable current error

chunks.title: Verify the measurement system
chunks.text: Check instrument performance against its specifications. Characterize the offset and leakage of the entire system before interpreting very small currents.
chunks.tags: verify verification noise floor instrument specification

chunks.title: Breakdown is a different experiment
chunks.text: A breakdown measurement increases reverse voltage until a specified test current is reached. It is distinct from measuring leakage at a fixed voltage.
chunks.tags: breakdown reverse voltage sweep avalanche test current

chunks.title: High-voltage procedures need specific controls
chunks.text: The high-voltage application note describes enclosing exposed conductors and following instrument safety requirements. This demo implements no physical hardware connection.
